attempted_axis: Verify the recorded claim that CTriListCollide's residual is `mr r23,r6` against `addi r23,r6,0` and is therefore the cheapest unconditional member of the copy-form family, before authoring a rule for it.

attributes.law_screen: claim.law.webfrank-cannot-close-instruction-count-deltas.20260831.v1 SCREENED and PASSED on the cheap test: 175/175, count-symmetric, so the count screen does not disqualify it and the premise had to be refuted on other evidence. claim.law.unpaired-schedule-words-bar-webfrank-candidacy-not-just-its-permute-stage.20260831.v1 APPLIED and DECISIVE: the function's residual is a displaced block, so it is barred from webfrank candidacy outright regardless of any form reasoning. claim.law.live-zero-copy-vs-remat-is-allocator-not-source.20260831.v1 and claim.law.constant-copy-vs-rematerialize-is-source-unreachable.20260831.v1 SCREENED and found NOT APPLICABLE here — neither side's differing word is a constant load, so this is not the live-zero family at all. The AGENTS.md aligned-view rule ('NEVER eyeball target and ours at the same absolute offset') APPLIED as the method that exposed the error. No source axis was probed: attempt.ctri-list-collide-entry-home-closure.20260831.v1 already caps the entry parameter-home/schedule axis as STRUCTURAL after five target-backed forms, and that cap is a VETO this session respected.
attributes.residual: UNCHANGED at 175/175, real 14; no edit was made. The residual is an ENTRY-SCHEDULE DISPLACEMENT, not a form pair: `fndiff --ops` reports one insert and one delete of a four-instruction block, our ['addi','lfs','lfd','mr'] at +0x2c-0x3c against target's ['mr','lfs','lfd','mr'] at +0x38-0x48, i.e. a run of parameter-home copies and float pool loads sitting three slots earlier in our build. The aligned fnasm --diff read shows that at +0x4c the target has `mr r23,r6` while OURS has `mr r22,r5` — both `mr`, differing only in registers — so there is no mr-versus-addi pair at any paired position. The `addi` the record's premise pointed at is our +0x2c word, which is `addi r30,r18,lbl_8023CA40@l`, an ADDR16_LO-RELOCATED ADDRESS COMPUTATION and not a register copy at all; rewriting it would be a relocation-payload change, which the tool contract forbids outright and which the new class's own no-relocation precondition refuses. Correct classification: SCHEDULE plus recolor, ineligible for every SINGLE-STAGE WebFrank rule while the displacement stands (a composed permute+form+recolor rule is not excluded, and per claim.law.RQ_webfrank-audit-silence-is-not-ineligibility.20260901.v1 an audit silence must not be read as a verdict here). STANDING DISCREPANCY for the integrator to arbitrate: lane CT's taxonomy (claim.CT_form-class-site-taxonomy-for-the-livezero-lane.20260901.v1) reportedly classifies this function as the roster's only class-(a) unconditional site, and the parent triage record described it as `mr r23,r6` against `addi r23,r6,0`. Both readings are consistent with a NAIVE SAME-OFFSET comparison and both are refuted by the aligned read reproduced above; the image-wide census independently paired no unconditional site here. If CT's taxonomy is accepted unamended, the two records will disagree, and this one carries the aligned evidence. The practical consequence is that the v1 unconditional rule has NO customer at all rather than exactly one.
